ROOT: FIXED-NETWORK UNARY FACET COMPLEXITY FROM ACTUAL-CLASS LOCAL WITNESSES
9 November 2026. New composition of accepted global Presburger class access, ROOT marked-coordinate balancing/local witnesses and the accepted conservative avatar. This is a mathematical support-geometry theorem, not the FULL inverse-height theorem or an independent novelty claim.

PREMISES / SCOPE.
Fix an actual SCC class Gamma of fixed R on N^d. Accepted ROOT marked-coordinate proof (90f5098edd8e35f18e635c4df12d3493bbc6c35373f9de2d45643bb34a3ce9b7) gives computable H_R>=1 such that EVERY m in CLOSED conv(Gamma) has an exact mean witness supported on Gamma intersect [m-H_R,m+H_R]^d. Extraction for rational m is polynomial COMPLETE-BINARY. All source/access/transfer/resource holds remain. No buffered-lattice replacement or Gibbs-law transfer is assumed.

1. CLOSED RATIONAL POLYHEDRA.
The global fixed Presburger predicate gives an effective finite semilinear representation of each class, Gamma=union_j(a_j+sum_k N b_jk), with nonnegative integer anchors and periods. No polynomial query cost for producing this whole representation is asserted here.
Let Q=conv{a_j}+cone{b_jk}. This is a closed rational polyhedron. Gamma subset Q, so closedconv(Gamma) subset Q.
Conversely each anchor is in Gamma. Each period b is a recession direction of closedconv(Gamma): for any x in this closed convex hull and t>=0,
 (1-t/n)x+(t/n)(a+n b)
belongs to the hull for integer n>=t and tends to x+t b. Thus Q subset closedconv(Gamma).
The local-witness theorem puts EVERY point of closedconv(Gamma) in conv(Gamma), so P=conv(Gamma)=Q is CLOSED. This last step is material: general semilinear sets need not have closed convex hulls.
P is pointed because P subset R_+^d. Its vertices are integral (vertices of conv anchors plus a pointed cone are among the anchors).

2. EVERY EDGE/RAY DIRECTION HAS A SHORT INTEGER REPRESENTATIVE.
Let F be a one-dimensional face of P, bounded edge or unbounded edge ray. Choose a noninteger m in its relative interior. The local witness for m lies entirely in F: any supporting linear functional defining F attains its extremum at m, and a convex combination of points in P can attain it only when every positive-weight point lies on the same face. For a face of higher codimension impose its defining supporting functionals together.
The witness cannot have only one distinct integer point si
